82	### 2.1 Index discipline: pointed covers, arbitrary opens
83	
84	```lean
85	/-- A pointed open cover of a scheme: one open per point, containing it. -/
86	structure Scheme.PointedCover (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
87	  opens : X → X.Opens
88	  mem_opens : ∀ x, x ∈ opens x
89	```
90	
91	with the refinement preorder `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`.
92	
93	Decision rationale (each alternative was weighed):
94	
95	- **Not finite covers, not affine covers, not `Set X.Opens`.** Pointed covers give:
96	  (a) *smallness for free* — the index type is the fixed carrier `X : Type u`, so the sigma type
97	  in §2.3 stays in `Type u`; (b) *canonical refinement maps* — a refinement `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰` refines
98	  **indexwise** (`𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`), so the cocycle-restriction map needs no choice of a
99	  reindexing function and no "independence of the refinement map" lemma at the carrier level;
100	  (c) *directedness by pointwise `⊓`* (`(𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens x := 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x`), so the
101	  refinement colimit is filtered; (d) *clean pullback* — for `f : X ⟶ Y` the pulled-back cover is
102	  `x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens (f x))`, again pointed, again indexed by the carrier. Affineness
103	  constraints would break (d) (preimages of affines are not affine); `Set`-indexing breaks (b)
104	  (pullback collapses indices).
105	- Affine or finite covers re-enter as *cofinality lemmas*, not as carrier structure: every
106	  pointed cover is refined by a pointed affine cover (`x ↦` an affine open neighbourhood inside
107	  `𝒰.opens x`; the choice lives inside a `Prop`, so no data escapes). This is where the
108	  2-cover computations of the χ-ledger and the T₀ engine plug in.

110	### 2.2 The cocycle layer: build on `PresheafOfGroups.H1`
111	
112	**Decision: build on mathlib's fixed-family layer**, not hand-rolled. Instantiation:
113	
114	```lean
115	/-- The units presheaf of a scheme, on its small Zariski site. -/
116	def Scheme.unitsPresheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} :=
117	  X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat ⋙ CommMonCat.units
118	-- (OPEN-4: if the `forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat` path is absent in v4.31, a ~20-line
119	-- bespoke functor replaces the composition; the statement shape is unchanged.)
120	
121	abbrev Scheme.unitsCocycle (X : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) :=
122	  PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) 𝒰.opens
123	```
124	
125	Here the site category is the poset `X.Opens`, the family is `𝒰.opens : X → X.Opens`, and
126	mathlib's `OneCochain/OneCocycle/OneCohomologyRelation/IsCohomologous/H1` + `One (H1 G U)`
127	(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/NonabelianCohomology/H1.lean:58–197`) come for free. On a poset
128	with infima, the `ev (i j) (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j)`-style cochain is *equivalent* to the
129	classical pair data `g x y ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y)` with the cocycle condition on triple infima: homs
130	are subsingletons, so `ev` is determined by its value at `T = 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y` via `ev_precomp`, and
131	`ev_trans` at the triple infimum is the classical condition. **Binding ergonomic requirement**:
132	`Picard/CechH1.lean` must provide the two-way bridge so lane agents never touch `ev` directly:
133	
134	```lean
135	/-- Build a 1-cocycle over a poset with binary infima from classical pair data. -/
136	def PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.ofPairs
137	    (g : ∀ x y, G.obj (op (𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒰.opens y)))
138	    (hg : ∀ x y z, /- restrictions to the triple infimum satisfy g x y · g y z = g x z -/) :
139	    OneCocycle G 𝒰.opens
140	lemma ev_inf (γ : OneCocycle G 𝒰.opens) (x y) : γ.ev x y ⋯ = ⋯   -- extraction at the infimum
141	```
142	
143	Additions ours to make (all in `Picard/CechH1.lean`, stated generically over any `Cᵒᵖ ⥤
144	CommGrpCat.{w}` — a mathlib-PR candidate, their file's TODO list asks for exactly this):
145	
146	- `Mul/Inv/CommGroup (OneCocycle Gc U)` when the presheaf is commutative-group-valued (the
147	  product of cocycles satisfies `ev_trans` only using commutativity), and the descended
148	  `CommGroup (H1 Gc U)` via `Quot.map₂` (compatibility of `IsCohomologous` with products again
149	  uses commutativity).
150	- Restriction along an indexwise refinement `res : H1 G 𝒰 →* H1 G 𝒱` for `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰`
151	  (on cocycles: restrict values along the inclusions; strictly functorial:
152	  `res_res : res h₂ ∘ res h₁ = res (h₁.trans h₂)` holds on the nose at cochain level).

154	### 2.3 The refinement colimit
155	
156	```lean
157	/-- The definitional Picard group: Čech H¹ of the units presheaf, colimit over pointed covers. -/
158	def Scheme.CechPic (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u :=
159	  Quot (fun p q : (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, PresheafOfGroups.H1 ⋯ 𝒰.opens) =>
160	    ∃ 𝒲, ∃ (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1), res h₁ p.2 = res h₂ q.2)
161	```
162	
163	- The relation is an equivalence *because the poset is directed* (common refinement by pointwise
164	  `⊓`) and `res` strictly composes; the standard filtered-colimit argument is elementary and
165	  choice-free.
166	- Universe accounting: `X.PointedCover : Type u`, each `H1 … : Type u` (index `X : Type u`,
167	  values in `Type u`), the sigma is `Type u`, the quotient is `Type u`. **No `ULift` anywhere.**
168	- `CommGroup (X.CechPic)`: multiplication of classes represented on a common refinement;
169	  well-definedness from §2.2's `CommGroup (H1 …)` + `res` being a group hom.
170	- Constructor/eliminator API: `CechPic.mk (𝒰) (γ : OneCocycle …) : X.CechPic`,
171	  `CechPic.ind`, `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff_of_refines`, and the "sanity gate"
172	  `CechPic (Spec (.of K)) ≃* PUnit`-style triviality for fields (one-point space, one cover,
173	  `ev_refl` kills every cocycle) — this is Lane 1's cheap end-to-end test.
174	
175	### 2.4 Group structure: multiplicative, `CommGrpCat`-valued
176	
177	**Decision: multiplicative.** Justification (each item load-bearing):
178	
179	1. The cocycle values are *units of rings*; their native structure is multiplicative, and
180	   `tensor product of line bundles = pointwise multiplication of transition units`,
181	   `dual = pointwise inverse` — recon lesson 1's entire point. An additive carrier would
182	   re-introduce a translation layer at exactly the spot the old draft burned.
183	2. `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` takes `F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}` — multiplicative — and
184	   `forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` is the canonical bridge. The old draft's
185	   `AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}` choice cost both a universe bump and an additive/multiplicative
186	   mismatch at the representability gate.
187	3. Mathlib's `PresheafOfGroups.H1` layer (§2.2) is multiplicative.
188	
189	The `ℤ`-valued *degree* (§6) is additive; the interface between the multiplicative Pic and the
190	additive degree is a single `→ ℤ` map with `deg (a * b) = deg a + deg b` — pinned as such, no
191	`Multiplicative ℤ` gymnastics in consumer-facing statements.
192	
193	### 2.5 Functoriality: pullback of cocycles
194	
195	```lean
196	def Scheme.CechPic.map {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic
197	theorem Scheme.CechPic.map_id (X) : CechPic.map (𝟙 X) = MonoidHom.id _
198	theorem Scheme.CechPic.map_comp (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
199	    CechPic.map (f ≫ g) = (CechPic.map f).comp (CechPic.map g)
200	```
201	
202	On representatives: pull the cover back pointwise through `f.base` (`x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f x)`),
203	pull the units back through `f.app`, restrict. `map_comp` compares the covers
204	`(f ≫ g) ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰 (g (f x))` and `f ⁻¹ᵁ (g ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰 (g (f x)))` — equal opens
205	(`Scheme.preimage_comp`), with the value comparison through `Scheme.Hom.app_comp`; if defeq
206	friction appears, prove it through the refinement relation (both sides restrict to a common
207	refinement) rather than `eqToHom` surgery.

209	### 2.6 Divisor classes as cocycles: the `𝒪(D)` constructor
210	
211	Three constructors, in dependency order. Sign convention (route §3, audited in §8):
212	a local-equation system `(fᵢ)` for an effective `D` produces the class of `𝒪(D)` with
213	transition units `g x y = f x / f y` on overlaps (trivialization of `𝒪(D)` on `𝒰x` by
214	multiplication by `f x`).
215	
216	**(a) Local-equation data → class** (`Picard/DivisorClass.lean`):
217	
218	```lean
219	/-- Local equations for an effective Cartier divisor, adapted to a pointed cover. -/
220	structure Scheme.LocalEquations (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
221	  cover : X.PointedCover
222	  eqn : ∀ x, Γ(X, cover.opens x)
223	  regular : ∀ x, /- eqn x is a nonzerodivisor in every stalk over cover.opens x -/
224	  ratio_isUnit : ∀ x y, IsUnit (/- (eqn x)/(eqn y) as a section on the overlap, i.e.
225	      ∃ u : unit on 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y, (eqn x)|∩ = u * (eqn y)|∩ -/)
226	
227	def Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass (d : X.LocalEquations) : X.CechPic
228	  -- the class of the cocycle (x,y) ↦ the unit u x y with (eqn x)|∩ = u x y • (eqn y)|∩
229	```
230	
231	with: uniqueness of `u x y` (regularity makes the ratio unit unique — this is why `regular` is
232	part of the data), the cocycle identity for `u` (from associativity of the ratios),
233	*independence*: two `LocalEquations` cutting out the same closed subscheme (or related by
234	unitwise rescaling) have equal `picClass`; *multiplicativity*: pointwise product of equations ↦
235	product of classes; *pullback compatibility*: for `f : X' ⟶ X` such that the pulled-back
236	equations are still regular (guaranteed in the relative situation below),
237	`(d.pullback f).picClass = CechPic.map f d.picClass`.
238	
239	**(b) The two geometric instances** (`Picard/GraphDivisor.lean`):
240	
241	- *Point divisor.* For a `k`-point `P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C`, the image of `P` is an
242	  effective Cartier divisor on `C.left`: the local ring at the image point is a DVR
243	  (`Curve/StalksDVR.lean`, Wave 1), so a uniformizer spreads to a local equation, and away from
244	  the point the equation `1` works. Output: `pointDivisor P : C.left.LocalEquations` (cover:
245	  a distinguished pointed cover; the choice of uniformizer is data *inside* the construction,
246	  with `picClass`-level independence proven — see the choice-discipline note in §4.4).
247	- *Graph divisor.* The diagonal `Δ ⊂ (C ⊗ C).left` is a relative effective divisor over the
248	  **second** factor: `pr₂|Δ` is an isomorphism onto the base, in particular finite flat of rank
249	  1, and smoothness of `C/k` of relative dimension 1 makes the conormal module invertible, so
250	  the ideal of `Δ` is locally one regular equation. Deliverable:
251	
252	  ```lean
253	  def graphLocalEquations (t : T ⟶ C /- in Over (Spec k) -/) :
254	      ((C ⊗ T).left).LocalEquations   -- local equations for Γ_t := (C ◁ t)-pullback of Δ ⋯
255	  theorem graphLocalEquations_base_change ⋯  -- Γ_{t ∘ g} equations = pullback of Γ_t equations
256	  ```
257	
258	  The base-change stability is *by construction*: `Γ_t` is the pullback of the universal `Δ`
259	  along `C ◁ (t ≫ ⋯)`, and (a)'s pullback compatibility applies because `Δ` is a *relative*
260	  divisor over the test factor (fibers never contain a component of `C`), so regularity
261	  survives every base change. Rank certificate: `𝒪_{Γ_t} ≅ 𝒪_T` as `T`-algebras, so the
262	  finite-flat rank of `Γ_t → T` is 1 — the input for the degree of `abelElement` (§6).
263	  This mathematics is Kleiman `ex:DivC` (§3.8: `X₀ = Div¹_{X/S}` for the smooth locus) and
264	  `rmk:Jac` (§5.26: "Given `t : T → X`, its graph subscheme `Γ_t ⊂ X × T` is a relative
265	  effective divisor"); both read.
266	
267	**(c) The meromorphic bridge** (`Picard/MeromorphicTrivialization.lean`; needed by the degree,
268	see §6.1): for `X` *integral*, every `CechPic` class is a divisor class. Cocycle proof shape:
269	every nonempty open contains the generic point; fix a base index `x₀` and localize the cocycle
270	values `g x x₀` into the function field; these are meromorphic local equations for a Cartier
271	divisor whose class is the given one. (Classical statement: Kleiman quotes it in the proof of
272	`th:qpp&p` (§5.4): "Since `X × T` is integral, there is a divisor `D` such that `𝒪(D) = 𝓛`
273	by [Hartshorne, Ex. II 6.15]".) This file also pins `divisorClass` for *differences*
274	`D₁ − D₂` of effective data as `picClass D₁ * (picClass D₂)⁻¹`.

94	  /-- The member of the cover attached to a point. -/

18	  of `Σ 𝒰, X.unitsH1 𝒰` by agreement on a common refinement, with its `CommGroup`
19	  structure and the constructor/eliminator API `CechPic.mk`, `CechPic.ind`,
20	  `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff`, `CechPic.mk_unitsRes`, `CechPic.mk_mul_mk_inf`.

25	  subsingleton underlying space (e.g. `Spec` of a field) the Picard group is trivial.

132	  mul_one a := by
133	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
134	    show mk (𝒰 ⊓ ⊤) (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right (1 : X.unitsH1 ⊤))
135	      = mk 𝒰 a
136	    rw [map_one, mul_one, mk_unitsRes]
137	  inv_mul_cancel a := by
138	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
139	    show mk (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰) (unitsRes inf_le_left a⁻¹ * unitsRes inf_le_right a) = mk ⊤ 1
140	    have h : unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰 ≤ 𝒰) a⁻¹
141	        * unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰 ≤ 𝒰) a = 1 := by
142	      rw [map_inv]
143	      exact inv_mul_cancel _
144	    rw [h]
145	    exact Quotient.sound ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰, le_rfl, le_top, by rw [map_one, map_one]⟩
146	  mul_comm a b := by
147	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
148	    induction b using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
149	    show mk (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱) (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right b)
150	      = mk (𝒱 ⊓ 𝒰) (unitsRes inf_le_left b * unitsRes inf_le_right a)
151	    refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱, le_rfl, le_inf inf_le_right inf_le_left, ?_⟩
152	    simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_unitsRes, unitsRes_rfl]
153	    exact mul_comm _ _
154	
155	lemma one_def : (1 : X.CechPic) = mk ⊤ 1 :=
156	  rfl
157	
158	/-- Multiplication of Picard classes on representatives: restrict both to the common
159	refinement `𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱` and multiply there. Holds by definition. -/
160	lemma mk_mul_mk_inf {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) (b : X.unitsH1 𝒱) :
161	    mk 𝒰 a * mk 𝒱 b
162	      = mk (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱) (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right b) :=
163	  rfl
164	
165	@[simp]
166	lemma mk_one (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) : mk 𝒰 (1 : X.unitsH1 𝒰) = 1 :=
167	  Quotient.sound ⟨𝒰, le_rfl, le_top, by rw [map_one, map_one]⟩
168	
169	@[simp]
170	lemma mk_mul_mk (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a b : X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
171	    mk 𝒰 a * mk 𝒰 b = mk 𝒰 (a * b) := by
172	  rw [mk_mul_mk_inf]
173	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰, le_rfl, inf_le_left, ?_⟩
174	  simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_rfl]
175	
176	@[simp]
177	lemma mk_inv (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) : (mk 𝒰 a)⁻¹ = mk 𝒰 a⁻¹ :=
178	  rfl
179	
180	/-! ## Functoriality: pullback of Picard classes -/
181	
182	private def mapSig (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : Σ 𝒰 : Y.PointedCover, Y.unitsH1 𝒰) :
183	    Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰 :=
184	  ⟨p.1.pullback f, f.pullbackUnitsH1 p.1 p.2⟩
185	
186	private lemma mapSig_compat (f : X ⟶ Y) :
187	    ∀ {p q : Σ 𝒰 : Y.PointedCover, Y.unitsH1 𝒰}, p ≈ q → mapSig f p ≈ mapSig f q := by
188	  rintro ⟨𝒰, a⟩ ⟨𝒱, b⟩ ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
189	  refine ⟨𝒲.pullback f, PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₁,
190	    PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₂, ?_⟩
191	  show unitsRes (PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₁) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a)
192	      = unitsRes (PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₂) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒱 b)
193	  rw [Hom.unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1 f h₁ a, Hom.unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1 f h₂ b, e]
194	
195	/-- Contravariant functoriality of the Čech Picard group: pull the cover back pointwise,
196	pull the unit cocycles back through `f`, restrict. -/
197	def map (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic where
198	  toFun := Quotient.map (mapSig f) fun _ _ h ↦ mapSig_compat f h
199	  map_one' := by
200	    show mk ((⊤ : Y.PointedCover).pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 ⊤ 1) = 1
201	    rw [map_one, mk_one]
202	  map_mul' a b := by
203	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
204	    induction b using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
205	    show mk ((𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).pullback f)
206	        (f.pullbackUnitsH1 (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱) (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right b))
207	      = mk (𝒰.pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a) *
208	          mk (𝒱.pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒱 b)
209	    rw [mk_mul_mk_inf]
210	    refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨(𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).pullback f, le_rfl,
211	      le_inf (PointedCover.pullback_mono f inf_le_left)
212	        (PointedCover.pullback_mono f inf_le_right), ?_⟩
213	    simp only [map_mul, ← Hom.unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1, unitsRes_unitsRes, unitsRes_rfl]
214	
215	@[simp]
216	lemma map_mk (f : X ⟶ Y) (𝒰 : Y.PointedCover) (a : Y.unitsH1 𝒰) :
217	    map f (mk 𝒰 a) = mk (𝒰.pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a) :=
218	  rfl
219	
220	/-- Pullback of Picard classes along the identity is the identity. -/
221	@[simp]
222	theorem map_id (X : Scheme.{u}) : map (𝟙 X) = MonoidHom.id X.CechPic := by
223	  refine MonoidHom.ext fun x ↦ ?_
224	  induction x using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
225	  show mk (𝒰.pullback (𝟙 X)) ((𝟙 X : X ⟶ X).pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a) = mk 𝒰 a
226	  have hle : 𝒰.pullback (𝟙 X) ≤ 𝒰 := fun x ↦ le_of_eq (by simp)
227	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰.pullback (𝟙 X), le_rfl, hle, ?_⟩
228	  induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
229	  refine congrArg (Quot.mk _) ?_
230	  ext x y T a b
231	  rw [OneCocycle.res_ev, OneCocycle.res_ev, Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_ev,
232	    γ.toOneCochain.ev_eq_evInf]
233	  exact id_unitsAppLE _ _
234	
235	/-- Pullback of Picard classes along a composite (the lane keystone). -/
236	theorem map_comp (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : map (f ≫ g) = (map f).comp (map g) := by
237	  refine MonoidHom.ext fun x ↦ ?_
238	  induction x using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
239	  show mk (𝒰.pullback (f ≫ g)) ((f ≫ g).pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a)
240	    = mk ((𝒰.pullback g).pullback f)
241	        (f.pullbackUnitsH1 (𝒰.pullback g) (g.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a))
242	  have hle : 𝒰.pullback (f ≫ g) ≤ (𝒰.pullback g).pullback f := fun x ↦ le_of_eq (by simp)
243	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰.pullback (f ≫ g), le_rfl, hle, ?_⟩
244	  induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
245	  refine congrArg (Quot.mk _) ?_
246	  ext x y T a b
247	  rw [OneCocycle.res_ev, OneCocycle.res_ev, Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_ev,
248	    Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_ev, Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_unitsEvInf, unitsAppLE_unitsAppLE]
249	  rfl
250	
251	/-! ## Sanity gate: triviality over a field -/
252	
253	/-- On a scheme with a subsingleton underlying space — e.g. `Spec` of a field — the
254	Čech Picard group is trivial: every pointed cover is a cover by a single open, on which
255	every unit cocycle is a coboundary. -/
256	instance subsingleton_of_subsingleton (X : Scheme.{u}) [Subsingleton X] :
257	    Subsingleton X.CechPic := by
258	  refine ⟨fun p q ↦ ?_⟩
259	  induction p using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
260	  induction q using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
261	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱, inf_le_left, inf_le_right, ?_⟩
262	  have := H1.subsingleton_of_forall_le (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat)
263	    (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens (fun i j ↦ le_of_eq (congrArg _ (Subsingleton.elim i j)))
264	  exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
265	
266	/-- The Čech Picard group of the spectrum of a field is trivial. -/
267	theorem eq_one_of_subsingleton (X : Scheme.{u}) [Subsingleton X] (x : X.CechPic) :
268	    x = 1 :=
269	  Subsingleton.elim x 1
270	
271	example {K : Type u} [Field K] (x : (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).CechPic) : x = 1 :=
272	  eq_one_of_subsingleton _ x
273	
274	end CechPic
275	
276	end Scheme

5	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

8	/-!
9	# The units presheaf of a scheme
10	
11	For a scheme `X`, this file defines the presheaf `𝒪_X^*` of unit groups of the structure
12	sheaf on the small Zariski site (the poset `X.Opens`), valued in `CommGrpCat`, together
13	with the element-level interface used by the Čech `H¹` layer of the Picard group:
14	
15	* restriction of a unit section along `V ≤ U` is `Units.map` of the ring-level restriction;
16	* pullback of a unit section along a morphism of schemes, packaged as
17	  `Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE` (the unit-group analogue of `Scheme.Hom.appLE`), with the same
18	  composition/restriction calculus as `appLE`.
19	
20	## Main declarations
21	
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsPresheaf`: the units presheaf
23	  `X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat ⋙ CommMonCat.units`, a functor
24	  `(X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}`.
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsPresheaf_map_apply`: restriction of unit sections,
26	  element form.
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE`: for `f : X ⟶ Y`, `V : Y.Opens`,
28	  `U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V`, the group homomorphism `Γ(Y, V)ˣ →* Γ(X, U)ˣ`.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map`, `Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE`,
30	  `Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_unitsAppLE`, `Scheme.id_unitsAppLE`: the calculus mirroring
31	  `appLE_map`, `map_appLE`, `appLE_comp_appLE` and `id_app` at the unit level.
32	-/
33	
34	set_option autoImplicit false
35	
36	universe u
37	
38	open CategoryTheory Opposite
39	
40	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
41	
42	namespace Scheme
43	
44	variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
45	
46	/-- The units presheaf `𝒪_X^*` of a scheme `X`, on its small Zariski site: the composite
47	of the structure presheaf with the units functor, valued in commutative groups.
48	
49	This is `abbrev` (reducible): the Čech layer constantly mixes sections typed through
50	`unitsPresheaf.obj` with sections typed `Γ(X, U)ˣ`, and rewriting across that boundary
51	requires the two to agree at instance transparency. -/
52	abbrev unitsPresheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} :=
53	  X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat ⋙ CommMonCat.units
54	
55	lemma unitsPresheaf_obj (U : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ) :
56	    X.unitsPresheaf.obj U = CommGrpCat.of Γ(X, unop U)ˣ :=
57	  rfl
58	
59	lemma unitsPresheaf_map {U V : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V) :
60	    X.unitsPresheaf.map i = CommGrpCat.ofHom (Units.map (X.presheaf.map i).hom) :=
61	  rfl
62	
63	/-- Element form of the restriction maps of the units presheaf. This is the interface
64	through which cocycle computations reach the `Units` API. -/
65	@[simp]
66	lemma unitsPresheaf_map_apply {U V : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V) (u : Γ(X, unop U)ˣ) :
67	    X.unitsPresheaf.map i u = Units.map (X.presheaf.map i).hom u :=
68	  rfl
69	
70	/-- The composite with the forgetful functor to `GrpCat` (the shape consumed by
71	`CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle`), element form. -/
72	@[simp]
73	lemma unitsPresheaf_forget₂_map_apply {U V : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V) (u : Γ(X, unop U)ˣ) :
74	    (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).map i u
75	      = Units.map (X.presheaf.map i).hom u :=
76	  rfl
77	
78	/-- Split form of `unitsPresheaf_forget₂_map_apply`: after `Functor.comp_map` has fired,
79	the restriction maps appear as `(forget₂ _ _).map (X.unitsPresheaf.map i)`. -/
80	@[simp]
81	lemma forget₂_map_unitsPresheaf_map_apply {U V : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V)
82	    (u : Γ(X, unop U)ˣ) :
83	    (forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).map (X.unitsPresheaf.map i) u
84	      = Units.map (X.presheaf.map i).hom u :=
85	  rfl
86	
87	namespace Hom
88	
89	variable (f : X ⟶ Y) {V V' : Y.Opens} {U U' : X.Opens}
90	
91	/-- The action of a morphism of schemes on unit sections: for `V : Y.Opens` and
92	`U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V`, the induced group homomorphism `Γ(Y, V)ˣ →* Γ(X, U)ˣ`. This is the
93	unit-group analogue of `Scheme.Hom.appLE` and is treated as a suffix in lemma names. -/
94	def unitsAppLE (f : X.Hom Y) (V : Y.Opens) (U : X.Opens) (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) :
95	    Γ(Y, V)ˣ →* Γ(X, U)ˣ :=
96	  Units.map (f.appLE V U e).hom
97	
98	@[simp]
99	lemma coe_unitsAppLE (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (u : Γ(Y, V)ˣ) :
100	    (f.unitsAppLE V U e u : Γ(X, U)) = f.appLE V U e u :=
101	  rfl
102	
103	/-- Restriction after pullback: the unit-level mirror of `Scheme.Hom.appLE_map`. -/
104	@[simp]
105	lemma unitsAppLE_map (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (i : op U ⟶ op U') (u : Γ(Y, V)ˣ) :
106	    Units.map (X.presheaf.map i).hom (f.unitsAppLE V U e u)
107	      = f.unitsAppLE V U' (i.unop.le.trans e) u := by
108	  ext
109	  simp only [Units.coe_map, MonoidHom.coe_coe, coe_unitsAppLE]
110	  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, appLE_map]
111	
112	/-- Pullback after restriction: the unit-level mirror of `Scheme.Hom.map_appLE`. -/
113	@[simp]
114	lemma map_unitsAppLE (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (i : op V' ⟶ op V) (u : Γ(Y, V')ˣ) :
115	    f.unitsAppLE V U e (Units.map (Y.presheaf.map i).hom u)
116	      = f.unitsAppLE V' U (e.trans ((TopologicalSpace.Opens.map f.base).map i.unop).le) u := by
117	  ext
118	  simp only [Units.coe_map, MonoidHom.coe_coe, coe_unitsAppLE]
119	  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, map_appLE]
120	
121	end Hom
122	
123	/-- Pullback along a composite: the unit-level mirror of `Scheme.appLE_comp_appLE`. -/
124	@[simp]
125	lemma unitsAppLE_unitsAppLE (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) {W : Z.Opens} {V : Y.Opens}
126	    {U : X.Opens} (e₁ : V ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ W) (e₂ : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (u : Γ(Z, W)ˣ) :
127	    f.unitsAppLE V U e₂ (g.unitsAppLE W V e₁ u)
128	      = (f ≫ g).unitsAppLE W U
129	          (e₂.trans ((TopologicalSpace.Opens.map f.base).map (homOfLE e₁)).le) u := by
130	  ext
131	  simp only [Hom.coe_unitsAppLE]
132	  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, Hom.appLE_comp_appLE]
133	
134	/-- Pullback along the identity is restriction: the unit-level mirror of `Scheme.id_app`. -/
135	lemma id_unitsAppLE {U V : X.Opens} (e : U ≤ V) (u : Γ(X, V)ˣ) :
136	    (𝟙 X : X ⟶ X).unitsAppLE V U e u
137	      = Units.map (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE e).op).hom u :=
138	  rfl
139	
140	end Scheme

10	/-!
11	# Čech 1-cocycles: restriction, poset pair data, and commutative group structure
12	
13	This file extends Mathlib's fixed-family nonabelian Čech layer
14	(`CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle`, `H1`) with the three pieces of
15	infrastructure needed for a Čech-style Picard group (all stated generically; this file
16	is a Mathlib-PR candidate and contains no algebraic geometry):
17	
18	1. **Restriction along an indexwise refinement.** For families `U V : I → C` and maps
19	   `f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i`, cochains/cocycles/`H1`-classes restrict along `f`, strictly
20	   functorially (`res_res` holds on the nose at the cochain level).
21	2. **The poset bridge.** Over a poset with binary infima, a 1-cochain is determined by
22	   its values `evInf i j` at the infima `U i ⊓ U j` (`ev_eq_evInf`), and a 1-cocycle can
23	   be built from classical pair data satisfying the cocycle condition at triple infima
24	   (`OneCocycle.ofPairs`). Consumers never need to touch `ev` directly.
25	3. **Commutative group structure.** When the presheaf takes values in `CommGrpCat`,
26	   1-cocycles form a commutative group under pointwise multiplication (the cocycle
27	   condition for products needs commutativity) and this descends to `H1`; restriction
28	   is then a group homomorphism (`H1.resHom`).
29	
30	## Main declarations
31	
32	* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCochain.res`, `OneCocycle.res`, `H1.res`:
33	  restriction along an indexwise refinement, with `res_res` and `res_id`.
34	* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCochain.evInf`, `ev_eq_evInf`: over a poset with
35	  binary infima, evaluation of a cochain at `U i ⊓ U j` determines it.
36	* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.ofPairs`: the classical construction of a
37	  cocycle from pair data `g i j` on binary infima with the triple-infimum condition.
38	* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf`: the coboundary
39	  relation in classical pair form.
40	* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.H1.subsingleton_of_forall_le`: if the members of the
41	  family are mutually comparable (e.g. all equal to a top element), `H1` is trivial.
42	* `CommGroup (OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U)` and
43	  `CommGroup (H1 (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U)` for `G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat`.
44	* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.H1.resHom`: restriction as a group homomorphism.
45	-/

73	    (γ.res f).ev i j a b = γ.ev i j (a ≫ f i) (b ≫ f j) :=

194	    G.map (homOfLE h₁).op (G.map (homOfLE h₂).op x) = G.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op x := by

199	/-- The value of a 1-cochain on the binary infimum `U i ⊓ U j`. Over a poset with binary
200	infima this determines the whole cochain, see `ev_eq_evInf`. -/
201	def evInf (γ : OneCochain G U) (i j : I) : G.obj (op (U i ⊓ U j)) :=
202	  γ.ev i j (homOfLE inf_le_left) (homOfLE inf_le_right)

204	/-- Over a poset, a 1-cochain is determined by its values on binary infima. -/
205	lemma ev_eq_evInf (γ : OneCochain G U) (i j : I) {T : P} (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j) :
206	    γ.ev i j a b = G.map (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le)).op (γ.evInf i j) := by
207	  have h := γ.ev_precomp i j (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le))
208	    (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U i)) (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U j))
209	  rw [Subsingleton.elim (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le) ≫ homOfLE inf_le_left) a,
210	    Subsingleton.elim (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le) ≫ homOfLE inf_le_right) b] at h
211	  exact h.symm

214	lemma res_evInf {V : I → P} (γ : OneCochain G U) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) (i j : I) :
215	    (γ.res f).evInf i j
216	      = G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf (f i).le (f j).le)).op (γ.evInf i j) :=
217	  γ.ev_eq_evInf i j (homOfLE inf_le_left ≫ f i) (homOfLE inf_le_right ≫ f j)

234	infimum, `g i j * g j k = g i k`. -/
235	lemma evInf_trans (γ : OneCocycle G U) (i j k : I) :
236	    G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U i ⊓ U j)).op (γ.evInf i j) *
237	        G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U j ⊓ U k)).op
238	          (γ.evInf j k) =
239	      G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U i ⊓ U k)).op
240	        (γ.evInf i k) := by
241	  have h := γ.ev_trans i j k (T := U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k)
242	    (homOfLE (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left)) (homOfLE (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right))
243	    (homOfLE inf_le_right)
244	  simp only [γ.toOneCochain.ev_eq_evInf] at h
245	  exact h

248	`g i j` on the binary infima satisfying the cocycle condition on triple infima. -/
249	def ofPairs (g : ∀ i j, G.obj (op (U i ⊓ U j)))
250	    (hg : ∀ i j k,
251	      G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U i ⊓ U j)).op (g i j) *
252	          G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U j ⊓ U k)).op
253	            (g j k) =
254	        G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U i ⊓ U k)).op
255	          (g i k)) :
256	    OneCocycle G U where
257	  ev i j _ a b := G.map (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le)).op (g i j)
258	  ev_precomp i j T T' φ a b := map_map G φ.le (le_inf a.le b.le) (g i j)
259	  ev_trans i j k T a b c := by
260	    rw [← map_map G (le_inf (le_inf a.le b.le) c.le) inf_le_left (g i j),
261	      ← map_map G (le_inf (le_inf a.le b.le) c.le) (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right) (g j k),
262	      ← map_map G (le_inf (le_inf a.le b.le) c.le) (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left) (g i k),
263	      ← map_mul, hg i j k]

274	  change G.map (homOfLE (le_inf (homOfLE inf_le_left).le (homOfLE inf_le_right).le)).op (g i j)
275	      = g i j
276	  have h : homOfLE (le_inf (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U i)).le
277	      (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U j)).le) = 𝟙 (U i ⊓ U j) :=
278	    Subsingleton.elim _ _
279	  rw [h, op_id, G.map_id]

292	lemma isCohomologous_iff_evInf (γ₁ γ₂ : OneCocycle G U) :
293	    γ₁.IsCohomologous γ₂ ↔ ∃ α : ZeroCochain G U, ∀ i j,
294	      G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U i)).op (α i) * γ₁.evInf i j =
295	        γ₂.evInf i j * G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U j)).op (α j) := by
296	  constructor
297	  · rintro ⟨α, hα⟩
298	    exact ⟨α, fun i j ↦ hα i j (homOfLE inf_le_left) (homOfLE inf_le_right)⟩
299	  · rintro ⟨α, hα⟩
300	    refine ⟨α, fun i j T a b ↦ ?_⟩
301	    have h' := congrArg (G.map (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le : T ≤ U i ⊓ U j)).op ·) (hα i j)
302	    simp only [map_mul, map_map] at h'
303	    rw [γ₁.toOneCochain.ev_eq_evInf i j a b, γ₂.toOneCochain.ev_eq_evInf i j a b]

317	    | inr hI =>
318	      obtain ⟨i₀⟩ := hI
319	      refine ⟨fun i ↦ γ.ev i i₀ (𝟙 (U i)) (homOfLE (h i i₀)), fun i j T a b ↦ ?_⟩

328	    induction y using Quot.ind with
329	    | _ δ =>
330	      exact Quot.sound ((OneCocycle.equivalence_isCohomologous G U).trans

A local-equation system `(fᵢ)` for an effective divisor `D` — one regular section `fᵢ`
on each member `𝒰 i` of a pointed cover, agreeing up to a unit on overlaps — is the
data of a trivialization of the invertible sheaf `𝒪(D)`: on `𝒰 i` the sheaf `𝒪(D)` is
trivialized by multiplication by `fᵢ`. The resulting transition units are

`g i j = fᵢ / fⱼ ∈ Γ(X, 𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒰 j)ˣ`,

i.e. the unique unit with `fᵢ|∩ = g i j · fⱼ|∩`. The class of the corresponding Čech
1-cocycle is `𝒪(D)`; this is `Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass`.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations`: local-equation data for an effective
  Cartier divisor adapted to a pointed cover — a regular section on each member, with
  the overlap ratios being units.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors`: the
  section-level regularity consequence — every restriction of an equation to a sub-open
  is a nonzerodivisor.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.ratioUnit`, `ratioUnit_unique`,
  `ratioUnit_trans`: the transition units `g i j = fᵢ / fⱼ`, their uniqueness (from
  regularity), and the cocycle identity on triple overlaps.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.unitsCocycle`,
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass`: the Čech 1-cocycle `g i j` and its
  Picard class `𝒪(D)`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Opposite CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme

variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}}

/-! ## Ring-level restriction helpers -/

/-- Restriction of a section along `W ≤ V ≤ U` composes to restriction along `W ≤ U`. -/
private lemma sectionRestrict_comp {W V U : X.Opens} (h₁ : W ≤ V) (h₂ : V ≤ U)
    (s : Γ(X, U)) :
    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₁).op).hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₂).op).hom s)
      = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op).hom s := by
  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]

/-- The underlying section of a restricted unit is the ring-level restriction of its
underlying section. -/
private lemma coe_unitsRestrict {W U : X.Opens} (h : W ≤ U) (u : Γ(X, U)ˣ) :
    (X.unitsRestrict h u : Γ(X, W)) = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom (u : Γ(X, U)) := by
  simp only [Scheme.unitsRestrict, Units.coe_map, MonoidHom.coe_coe]

/-! ## Local equations -/

/-- Local equations for an effective Cartier divisor on `X`, adapted to a pointed cover:
a section `eqn x` on each member `cover.opens x`, whose germ at every point of that member
is a nonzerodivisor (`regular`) and whose overlap ratios `eqn x / eqn y` are units
(`ratio_isUnit`). The class of the associated Čech cocycle of transition units is the
divisor class `𝒪(D)`, see `LocalEquations.picClass`. -/
structure LocalEquations (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
  /-- The pointed cover on whose members the local equations live. -/
  cover : X.PointedCover
  /-- The local equation on the member `cover.opens x`. -/
  eqn : ∀ x, Γ(X, cover.opens x)
  /-- Each local equation is regular: its germ at every point of its member is a
  nonzerodivisor in the stalk. This is the primitive form of regularity; it implies the
  regularity of every restriction (`eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors`). -/
  regular : ∀ (x y : X) (hy : y ∈ cover.opens x),
    (X.presheaf.germ (cover.opens x) y hy).hom (eqn x) ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y)
  /-- On the overlap `cover.opens x ⊓ cover.opens y` the two equations differ by a unit
  factor `eqn x = u · eqn y`, so that `𝒪(D)` is invertible. -/
  ratio_isUnit : ∀ x y, ∃ u : Γ(X, cover.opens x ⊓ cover.opens y)ˣ,
    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn x)
      = (u : Γ(X, cover.opens x ⊓ cover.opens y))
        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (eqn y)

namespace LocalEquations

variable (d : X.LocalEquations)

/-- Section-level regularity: the restriction of `eqn x` to any sub-open `W ≤ cover.opens x`
is a nonzerodivisor in `Γ(X, W)`. Sections of a sheaf inject into the product of their
germs, so nonzerodivisibility of the germs (the field `regular`) propagates to every
restriction. -/
lemma eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors (x : X) {W : X.Opens} (hW : W ≤ d.cover.opens x) :
    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hW).op).hom (d.eqn x) ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, W) := by
  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_right]
  intro t ht
  apply TopCat.Presheaf.section_ext X.sheaf W t 0
  intro y hy
  rw [map_zero]
  have key : (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom t
      * (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hW).op).hom (d.eqn x)) = 0 := by
    rw [← map_mul, ht, map_zero]
  rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at key
  exact (mul_left_mem_nonZeroDivisors_eq_zero_iff (d.regular x y (hW hy))).mp
    (by rw [mul_comm] at key; exact key)

/-! ## The transition units -/

/-- The transition unit `g x y = eqn x / eqn y ∈ Γ(X, 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y)ˣ`: the unique unit with
`eqn x|∩ = g x y · eqn y|∩`. -/
noncomputable def ratioUnit (x y : X) : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ :=
  (d.ratio_isUnit x y).choose

/-- The defining property of the transition unit `g x y`: on the overlap,
`eqn x = g x y · eqn y`. -/
lemma eqn_restrict_eq (x y : X) :
    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (d.eqn x)
      = (d.ratioUnit x y : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y) :=
  (d.ratio_isUnit x y).choose_spec

/-- Uniqueness of the transition unit: any unit `u` with `eqn x = u · eqn y` on the
overlap equals `g x y`. Regularity of `eqn y` (its restriction is a nonzerodivisor) makes
the ratio unique. -/
lemma ratioUnit_unique (x y : X) (u : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ)
    (hu : (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (d.eqn x)
      = (u : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y)) :
    u = d.ratioUnit x y := by
  refine Units.ext ?_
  refine (mul_cancel_right_mem_nonZeroDivisors
    (d.eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors y (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y
      ≤ d.cover.opens y))).mp ?_
  rw [← hu, d.eqn_restrict_eq x y]

/-- The cocycle identity for the transition units, on the triple overlap
`𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y ⊓ 𝒰z`: `g x y · g y z = g x z`. Proved by multiplying through by the regular
`eqn z` and cancelling. Mirrors `Scheme.unitsEvInf_trans`. -/
lemma ratioUnit_trans (x y z : X) :
    X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
          d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
            ≤ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)
        (d.ratioUnit x y)
      * X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right :
          d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
            ≤ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z)
          (d.ratioUnit y z)
      = X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left :
          d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
            ≤ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens z)
          (d.ratioUnit x z) := by
  refine Units.ext ?_
  -- work at the level of underlying sections on the triple overlap
  rw [Units.val_mul, coe_unitsRestrict, coe_unitsRestrict, coe_unitsRestrict]
  -- cancel the regular restriction of `eqn z`
  refine (mul_cancel_right_mem_nonZeroDivisors
    (d.eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors z (inf_le_right :
      d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z ≤ d.cover.opens z))).mp ?_
  -- `g x z · eqn z = eqn x` on the triple overlap
  have hA := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left :
      d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
        ≤ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens z)).op).hom (d.eqn_restrict_eq x z)
  rw [map_mul, sectionRestrict_comp, sectionRestrict_comp] at hA
  -- `g y z · eqn z = eqn y` on the triple overlap
  have hB := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right :
      d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
        ≤ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z)).op).hom (d.eqn_restrict_eq y z)
  rw [map_mul, sectionRestrict_comp, sectionRestrict_comp] at hB
  -- `g x y · eqn y = eqn x` on the triple overlap
  have hC := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
      d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
        ≤ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d.eqn_restrict_eq x y)
  rw [map_mul, sectionRestrict_comp, sectionRestrict_comp] at hC
  rw [mul_assoc, hB, hC, hA]

/-! ## The cocycle and its Picard class -/

/-- The Čech 1-cocycle of transition units `g x y = eqn x / eqn y` of a local-equation
system. -/
noncomputable def unitsCocycle : X.unitsCocycle d.cover :=
  OneCocycle.ofPairs (fun x y ↦ d.ratioUnit x y) (fun x y z ↦ d.ratioUnit_trans x y z)

@[simp]
lemma unitsCocycle_evInf (x y : X) :
    unitsEvInf d.unitsCocycle x y = d.ratioUnit x y :=
  OneCocycle.ofPairs_evInf (fun x y ↦ d.ratioUnit x y) _ x y

/-- The Picard class `𝒪(D)` of a local-equation system for the effective divisor `D`:
the Čech class of the cocycle of transition units. -/
noncomputable def picClass : X.CechPic :=
  CechPic.mk d.cover d.unitsCocycle.class

end LocalEquations

end Scheme
